title: Cline CLI npm Package Compromised via Suspected Cache Poisoning Attack

reading.body:
An AI agent triaging GitHub issues for the open-source Cline project was given excessive permissions and no prompt injection safeguards. An attacker could craft a malicious issue title containing prompt injection instructions that would cause the AI agent to execute arbitrary code. This code execution could compromise GitHub's cache system and steal publishing credentials, potentially allowing distribution of malware through official package repositories to millions of developers.

The system was deployed without adequate human oversight of the AI agent's capabilities or constraints relative to its permissions. The vulnerability persisted from December 2025 to February 2026 because private security reports went unanswered. A fix was applied within one hour of public disclosure by removing the AI workflow and restricting access to release credentials. It is not established whether any malicious package was successfully published before the fix, though evidence suggests an actor may have attempted exploitation.

summary:
# Summary

Cline, an open-source AI coding tool used by millions of developers, had a critical security vulnerability in its GitHub Actions workflow between December 2025 and February 2026. The issue stemmed from an AI agent designed to automatically triage repository issues that was configured with excessive permissions and lacked proper safeguards. A researcher named Adnan Khan discovered that attackers could craft malicious issue titles containing prompt injection instructions to trick the AI into executing arbitrary code. This code execution could be weaponized to poison GitHub's cache system and steal publishing credentials, potentially allowing attackers to distribute malware to millions of developers through compromised Cline updates across VS Code Marketplace, OpenVSX, and NPM.

Khan attempted multiple times to privately report the vulnerability starting January 1st, 2026, but received no response from Cline's security team. After public disclosure on February 9th, the team fixed the vulnerability within one hour by removing the problematic AI workflow and making security improvements. Evidence suggests another actor may have attempted exploitation of the vulnerability while it remained active. Cline has since confirmed they rotated all credentials and removed caching from sensitive release workflows. Khan's research also indicates a separate threat actor obtained valid NPM and OpenVSX credentials for Cline, though no malicious updates were published.
